title: Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions
summary: We prove Erdős's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length. More quantitatively, for every fixed k ≥ 3, we show $`\displaystyle r_k(N)\le C_kN\exp\bigl(-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k}\bigr)`$ with $`C_k,c_k,\varepsilon_k\gt 0`$, where $`r_k(N)`$ is the largest size of a subset of $`\{1,\ldots,N\}`$ with no nonconstant k -term arithmetic progression.
family_title: Erdős’s reciprocal-sum conjecture and quasipolynomial Szemerédi bounds

review.reason: Proves Erdős's conjecture on arithmetic progressions in sets with divergent reciprocal sum.

discussion.author: Andrew Lott
discussion.text: Did you notice that the bound they autoformalized for Szemeredi is weaker than the advertised quasipolynomial bound (but still stronger than any power of log)? The formalized bound is e^(-c(loglogN)^(1+epsilon)). Still gets Erdos Turan but it’s not quasipolynomial
